title: Knight of Wands Tarot Card Meaning: Upright, Reversed & Love
description: Knight of Wands upright: action, adventure, passion; reversed: haste, scattered energy. Love, work, advice and Waite's 1911 text. Draw it for your question.
h1: Knight of Wands Tarot Card Meaning
image_alt: Knight of Wands, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: an armored rider on a rearing horse holds up a leafy wand, three pyramids on the sand below.
capsule: The Knight of Wands is the card of action, adventure and passion: energy that wants to move right now. Reversed, that drive turns into haste, stalled starts or plans dropped halfway. It is a lively, mostly welcome card whose risk is speed without a target. Asked for yes or no, it says yes: the horse is already rearing to charge.

blocks.heading: What is on the Knight of Wands card?
paragraphs: An armored rider sits on a horse that rears up on its hind legs, and the horse is the largest thing in the picture. Waite shows the Knight "as if upon a journey, armed with a short wand" and adds that, although he wears mail, he "is not on a warlike errand" (p. 174). In Waite's words, "he is passing mounds or pyramids" (p. 174).

On the 1909 card the horse is a pale sandy color with both front legs high in the air, and the wand in the rider's raised hand sprouts small green leaves. Orange plumes stream from his helmet and sleeves, his yellow tunic is patterned with black curling figures, and three pyramids rise from the sand at the lower left. Waite gives the horse a job of its own: its motion is "a key to the character of its rider" and suggests "the precipitate mood" (p. 174), a hasty, headlong one.

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about the Knight of Wands?
paragraphs: Waite's upright list (p. 174) is about going away: leaving, being absent, fleeing, setting off abroad, moving house, with a friendly young man as the figure behind it. In Waite's reversed list (p. 174) the journey becomes a break: splits, interruptions and discord.

Waite's extra list of meanings is blunter and simply calls it "a bad card" (p. 288); Arcana Diary does not read the Knight that way. Today the card keeps that movement and adds fire: nerve, desire and a taste for the unknown.

blocks.heading: What does the Knight of Wands mean upright?
paragraphs: A horse already in the air: the Knight of Wands is action that does not wait for permission. It stands for boldness, passion and the pull of adventure, the moment when an idea becomes a plan and the plan becomes a ticket, a phone call or a first step. Travel, a move or a fresh start in a new place belong here too, which echoes the departures in Waite's list (p. 174).

This Knight starts fast; finishing is another matter. If you can name the goal in one sentence, ride. If you cannot, choose a direction first, so the charge carries you somewhere instead of just away.

blocks.heading: What does the Knight of Wands mean reversed?
paragraphs: Reversed, the Knight of Wands can point to haste without a plan: scattered energy, many starts and few finishes, and frustration when the world does not move at your speed. Enthusiasm can flare and fade, leaving unfinished plans behind.

Waite's reversed words, interruption and discord among them (p. 174), fit this side; reading it as momentum gone sideways is a modern reading, not Waite's. Choose the one project that matters, finish a small piece of it, and let the rest wait.

blocks.heading: What does the Knight of Wands mean in love?
paragraphs: Passion is this card's first word in love: sparks, flirting, spontaneous plans and the thrill of something new. Without a partner, it often describes a bold, exciting stretch of meeting people, or your own wish to stop waiting and make a move.

For a couple, the Knight brings back adventure: a trip together, a shared plan, more play and less routine. Upside down, the intensity can come in bursts, or impatience can push a relationship faster than it wants to go. Ask whether what you feel has roots or is a spark of the moment, then act on what you truly want.

blocks.heading: What does the Knight of Wands mean for work and money?
paragraphs: Work under this card moves quickly: a new venture, a bold pitch, a job with travel, a sudden change of plans met with energy. It suits launching things and taking initiative; reversed, it describes projects started in a rush and left half done.

Money with the Knight comes and goes fast: spending on impulse, a costly adventure, cash that funds excitement more than plans. Reversed, the same speed means rushed money choices made before the numbers are clear.

blocks.heading: What is the advice of the Knight of Wands?
paragraphs: Say yes to one plan or invitation that excites you instead of thinking it over again. Then give the energy a target: write down where you want it to lead and what finished would look like. Movement with a destination is this Knight at his best.

blocks.heading: Is the Knight of Wands a yes or no card?
The Knight of Wands as a person and as feelings
paragraphs: Picture the Knight of Wands as a person and you get the adventurer: charming, restless, quick to act and slow to sit still, the one who suggests the road trip and is packed first. It can be you when you feel ready to go. As feelings, the card stands for passion and excitement: strong attraction, a rush of interest, the wish to act on it right away. Reversed, those feelings run hot and cold: impatience, mixed signals, interest that burns bright and then cools.

blocks.heading: The Knight of Wands with other cards

pairs.text: A spark and the rider who carries it: an idea that wants action now. Start, then pace yourself.
The fastest knight beside the slowest. Your drive works best with a steady routine behind it.
Charge, then rest. A pause keeps the fire from running out.
Passion meets a real connection: excitement shared by two people, not chased alone.

blocks.heading: Knight of Wands, Knight of Swords or Eight of Wands?
paragraphs: Waite describes the Knight of Swords "riding in full course, as if scattering his enemies" (p. 230), while his Knight of Wands rides out on a journey with no battle in mind (p. 174). Today the Knight of Swords means quick thinking and sharp words; the Knight of Wands is passion and adventure, more fire than argument.

Waite's Eight of Wands is "a flight of wands through an open country" (p. 182), with no rider at all. That card describes events speeding up; the Knight describes a person, or your own drive, setting things in motion.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about the Knight of Wands
paragraphs: Where do I want this energy to take me?
What have I already started that deserves to be finished first?
Which spontaneous yes would make me feel most alive right now?

faq.q: Is the Knight of Wands a good or bad card?
faq.a: Mostly good. It brings courage, momentum and an appetite for life, which helps almost any question that needs a first step. What it warns about is rushing: jumping into choices and then losing interest. Slow down just enough to aim, and its energy is on your side.

faq.q: Does the Knight of Wands mean travel or moving house?
faq.a: It can. Waite lists departure, emigration and change of residence for this card (p. 174), and travel, relocation and trips abroad still belong to it today. Whether that fits depends on your question; the card names a wish to go, not a date or a destination.

faq.q: Does the Knight of Wands mean he likes me?
faq.a: No card can speak for one particular person. In a feelings question, the traditional sense of this Knight is lively attraction and eagerness to act on it; upside down, interest that arrives in bursts. Words and actions you can actually see tell you far more.

waite.quote: Departure, absence, flight, emigration. A dark young man, friendly. Change of residence. Reversed: Rupture, division, interruption, discord.
